messages.subject: Spatial modeling of binary response outcome
parts:
Dear all

I am modelling dichotomous response data to explain geographical variation in my data. I have attached my method and below is a brief description of my model;

 Yij follows a Bernoulli distribution for a child k located in state i = 1, ...,37 with response either 0 or 1. Structured and unstructured random effects were added to account for unobserved influential factors that vary across the state. I have ran my code but got this error message; 'covariate' must match 'values',  and both must either be 'numeric', or 'factor'/'character'. 

Please kindly put me through here. Thank you

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial modeling of binary response outcome
parts:
Hi,

I would guess you have a covariate that is a factor, like


demo(Bym)
---- ~~~

Type <Return> to start :

> data(Germany)
> g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
> source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
> ## just make a duplicated column
> Germany = cbind(Germany,region.struct=Germany$region)

> # standard BYM model
> formula1 = Y ~ f(region.struct,model="besag",graph=g) +
+ f(region,model="iid")

> result1 = inla(formula1,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E)


## add the error....


> Germany$region.struct=as.factor(Germany$region.struct)
> result1 = inla(formula1,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E)
Error in inla(formula1, family = "poisson", data = Germany, E = E) :
In f(region.struct): 'covariate' must match 'values', and both must

for this model, 'region.struct' must be numeric.

H
